2026.race: 156 laps in 2026, and the biggest entry in twelve years
2026.note: Engel, Martin, Schiller and Stolz took the Winward Mercedes-AMG to 3,958.968 km in 24:05:27.664, the full distance with no stoppage. Luca Engstler had put the Red Bull Abt car on pole at 8:11.123. A total of 161 cars were entered, the largest list since 2014, and 159 of them started.

2025.race: 141 laps in 2025, and a win decided by a penalty
2025.note: The Manthey Porsche led almost the whole race and lost it late to a penalty, which handed the 53rd running to Rowe Racing — the only top-class BMW in the field. Farfus, Krohn, Marciello and van der Linde covered 3,578.3 km in 24:02:40.104 in fine conditions. Kévin Estre had taken pole for Manthey at 8:12.741.

2024.race: 50 laps in 2024, the shortest running there has been
2024.note: Rain and fog reduced the race to fifty laps, fewer than any other edition, and Feller, Marschall, Mies and Stippler were in front of it for Scherer Sport PHX in the Audi R8. It came a year after the longest race on record, which is the Eifel weather in two sentences.

2023.race: 162 laps in 2023, the longest race the event has run
2023.note: Fernández Laser, Pittard, Bamber and Heinemann took Frikadelli Racing to the greatest distance in the history of the race, and gave Ferrari its first win here at the same time. The following year the race ran fifty laps.

2022.race: 159 laps in 2022, at the fiftieth running
2022.note: Mies, Feller, Vervisch and Vanthoor won the anniversary race for Scherer Sport Team Phoenix in the Audi R8. Fifty runnings had taken fifty-two years, because 1974, 1975 and 1983 were never held.

2021.race: 58 laps in 2021, stopped overnight by weather
2021.note: Rain and fog halted the race through the night and it finished on fifty-eight laps, a record low at the time. Cairoli, Christensen, Estre and Kern were the Manthey Porsche crew that survived it.

2020.note: Catsburg, Sims and Yelloly won for Rowe Racing in the BMW M6 with a three-driver crew rather than the usual four, in a race broken up by the weather.

2019.race: 157 laps in 2019, one more than the car behind
2019.note: Kaffer, Stippler, Vanthoor and Vervisch won the 47th running for Audi Sport Team Phoenix over 20-23 June, finishing a single lap clear of the Mercedes-AMG in second.

2018.race: 135 laps in 2018, and a finish settled on the road
2018.note: Tandy, Makowiecki, Pilet and Lietz won the 46th running for Manthey Racing on 10-13 May, and the Black Falcon Mercedes behind them completed the same 135 laps. When two cars finish level on distance the order is decided by who crosses the line first.

2017.race: 158 laps in 2017, with the second-placed car on the same number
2017.note: De Phillippi, Mies, Winkelhock and van der Linde won the 45th running for Audi Sport Team Land on 25-28 May, ahead of a BMW M6 that also finished on 158 laps. Sixty-four cars were classified.

2016.race: a race red-flagged by hail in 2016
2016.note: A hailstorm caused a series of crashes and stopped the race. Engel, Schneider, Christodoulou and Metzger won it for AMG Team Black Falcon, and Mercedes filled the first four places.

2015.note: Müller, Sandström, Vanthoor and Mies won the 43rd running for Audi Sport Team WRT on 14-17 May in the R8 LMS.

2014.race: 159 laps in 2014, a distance record at the time
2014.note: Haase, Mamerow, Rast and Winkelhock set the longest distance the race had then seen, for Phoenix Racing in the Audi R8 LMS ultra. René Rast would go on to win three DTM titles.

2013.race: 158 laps in 2013, and a first win for Mercedes
2013.note: Schneider, Bleekemolen, Edwards and Thiim gave Mercedes-Benz its first victory in the race, for Black Falcon in the SLS AMG GT3. Bernd Schneider had already won five DTM championships by then.

2012.race: 155 laps in 2012, at the fortieth running
2012.note: Basseng, Haase, Stippler and Winkelhock won for Audi Sport Team Phoenix on 19-20 May. A new qualifying format sent the forty fastest teams out on the Friday, and the field was capped at 190 entries, down from 250 the year before.

2011.race: 156 laps in 2011, a distance record at the time
2011.note: Lieb, Bernhard, Luhr and Dumas set what was then the longest distance in the race, for Manthey Racing in the 997 GT3-RSR. It was a fifth win for Bernhard, who shares the record for most victories.

2010.note: Jörg Müller, Alzen, Farfus and Lamy won for BMW Motorsport and Schnitzer in the M3 GT2. It was a fifth win for Pedro Lamy, who shares the record for most victories with Timo Bernhard and Marcel Tiemann.

2009.race: 147 laps in 2009, a third consecutive win for the same team
2009.note: Dumas, Lieb, Bernhard and Tiemann won for Manthey Racing in the 997 GT3-RSR, completing three in a row for the team and very nearly the same four drivers.

2008.note: Lieb, Bernhard, Tiemann and Dumas won for Manthey Racing in the 997 GT3-RSR, the second of the team’s three consecutive victories.

2007.race: eighteen hours of racing in 2007, after six hours of fog
2007.note: Fog stopped the race for six hours and only eighteen of the twenty-four were run. Dumas, Lieb, Bernhard and Tiemann won it for Manthey Racing.

2006.race: 151 laps in 2006, a distance record set in good conditions
2006.note: Luhr, Bernhard, Rockenfeller and Tiemann took the Manthey Porsche 996 GT3-MR to the longest distance the race had run to that point. Mike Rockenfeller would win the DTM title seven years later.

2005.race: 139 laps in 2005, and the last race of the BMW M3 GTR
2005.note: Said, Huisman, Priaulx and Lamy won the 33rd running on 7-8 May, Schnitzer’s fifth victory here and its second consecutive one-two — something no team had done before. The M3 GTR retired from racing with the win, in front of 180,000 people, and Huisman reported snow on his final laps. The course had been modified that year to 25.378 km a lap, so distances before and after are not comparable.

2004.race: a BMW one-two in 2004, at the 32nd running
2004.note: Lamy, Dirk Müller, Jörg Müller and Stuck won on 12-13 June for BMW Motorsport, run by Schnitzer under Charly Lamm with BMW’s own engineers, and the team took the first two places. It was BMW’s seventeenth overall victory in the race, and a second for Stuck thirty-four years after his first.

2003.race: a win for a touring car in 2003, against sports cars
2003.note: Reuter, Scheider and Tiemann won in the Opel Astra V8 Coupé for OPC Team Phoenix, a three-driver crew in a car built to DTM-adjacent rules rather than a GT machine. Manuel Reuter had won the last DTM title of the original era in 1996 and Timo Scheider would win two of the revived ones.

2002.race: a second consecutive Viper win in 2002
2002.note: Zakowski, Lechner and Lamy won for Zakspeed in the Chrysler Viper GTS-R, repeating the previous year’s result with the same car.

2001.note: Lamy, Zakowski and Bartels won for Zakspeed in the Chrysler Viper GTS-R, an American V10 taking on the German touring cars and Porsches on their own road.

2000.race: 145 laps in 2000, beating a ten-year-old distance record
2000.note: Mayländer, Bartels, Alzen and Heger won for Porsche Zentrum Koblenz, run by Phoenix Racing, in the 911 GT3-R, and went further than any crew since 1990. Bernd Mayländer later spent two decades driving the Formula One safety car.

1999.race: 143 laps in 1999, with the fast cars back
1999.note: Zakowski, Hans-Jürgen Tiemann, Ludwig and Duez won for Zakspeed in the Chrysler Viper GTS-R, in the year powerful machinery returned to the entry. Klaus Ludwig had won three DTM titles and would take his second win here.

1998.race: 137 laps in 1998, and the first diesel win in a major 24-hour race
1998.note: Duez, Bovensiepen, Menzel and Stuck won in a BMW 320d for Schnitzer Motorsport — the first time a diesel took a major twenty-four hour race outright. It was a second win for Hans-Joachim Stuck, twenty-eight years after he won the first running of this race.

1997.note: Scheid, Schmitz, Hans-Jürgen Tiemann and Zakowski won for Scheid Motorsport in the BMW M3, a second consecutive win for Johannes Scheid and Sabine Schmitz.

1996.race: 135 laps in 1996, and the first win by a female driver
1996.note: Sabine Schmitz won with Johannes Scheid and Hans Widmann for Scheid Motorsport in a BMW M3, the first woman to win the race. She won it again the following year and became the best-known driver on this circuit.

1995.note: Ravaglia, Duez and Burgstaller won for Team Bigazzi in a BMW 320i. It was a third win here for Roberto Ravaglia, who had taken the 1989 DTM championship.

1994.note: Wlazik, Katthöfer and Rosterg won in a BMW M3, a short race by the standards of the decade either side of it.

1993.note: Katthöfer, de Azevedo, Konrad and Wirdheim won for Konrad Motorsport in a Porsche 911 Carrera, breaking a run of BMW victories.

1992.race: 76 laps in 1992, with the race stopped for hours in fog
1992.note: Fog held the race up long enough that the winners covered seventy-six laps, half what a clear year produced. Cecotto, Danner, Jean-Michel Martin and Duez won for Team Bigazzi in the M3 Evo. Johnny Cecotto had been a grand prix motorcycle world champion in 1975.

1991.note: Nissen, Winkelhock and Hahne won for Schnitzer Motorsport in the BMW M3 Evo, a second consecutive win for Joachim Winkelhock.

1990.race: 144 laps in 1990, a distance record that stood for a decade
1990.note: Heger, Winkelhock and Schmickler won for Linder Motorsport in the BMW M3 Evo, and no crew went further until 2000.

1989.note: Pirro, Ravaglia and Giroix won for Team Bigazzi in a BMW M3. Emanuele Pirro went on to win Le Mans five times.

1988.race: 140 laps in 1988, won by a privateer in a fourteen-year-old car
1988.note: Dören, Holup and Faubel won in a 1974 Porsche 911 Carrera RSR run by their own team, beating the modern factory-backed turbocharged Fords that had won the year before.

1987.race: 135 laps in 1987, and the first win for a turbocharged car
1987.note: Ludwig, Niedzwiedz and Soper won for Eggenberger Motorsport in the Ford Sierra RS Cosworth, the first turbo car to take the race. Klaus Ludwig would win the DTM title the following year.

1986.note: Oestreich, Rensing and Vogt won for the Auto Budde Team in a BMW 325i, the team’s third consecutive victory and its first with the smaller car.

1985.note: Felder, Hammelmann and Walterscheid-Müller won for the Auto Budde Team in the BMW 635 CSi, a second consecutive win for the team and for Axel Felder.

1984.race: 127 laps in 1984, the first running after a year off
1984.note: Felder, Bröhling and Oberndorfer won for the Auto Budde Team in a BMW 635 CSi. The 1983 race had not been held because of construction work at the circuit.

1982.note: Gartmann, Ludwig and Niedzwiedz won for Eichberg Racing in a Ford Capri, the same three-man shape and the same marque that had taken the previous year.

1981.note: Döring, Gartmann and Fritz Müller won for Gilden Kölsch in a Ford Capri. It was a fourth win for Müller, who had taken three in a row in Porsches in the 1970s.

1980.note: Selzer, Wolf and Matthias Schneider won in a Ford Escort RS 2000 for Berkenkamp Racing, a small car winning outright in the way this race has always allowed.

1979.note: Kummle, Mauer and Vogt won in a Ford Escort for Cavallo Matras, the second consecutive year a Ford took the race from the Porsches.

1978.note: Fritz Müller, Hechler and Geschwendtner won for Valvoline Deutschland in a Porsche 911 Carrera, a third consecutive win for Müller and Hechler together.

1977.race: 140 laps in 1977, won by a crew of two
1977.note: Fritz Müller and Herbert Hechler shared the Porsche 911 Carrera between just the two of them for twenty-four hours, and won for the second year running.

1976.race: 134 laps in 1976, the first running after two cancelled years
1976.note: Fritz Müller, Hechler and Quirin won in a Porsche 911 Carrera. The race had not been held in 1974 or 1975 because of the oil crisis.

1973.race: 95 laps in 1973, run as two eight-hour heats
1973.note: The race was split into two eight-hour heats with an eight-hour break at midnight, and Niki Lauda won it with Hans-Peter Joisten in an Alpina BMW 3.0 CSL. Lauda was two years away from the first of his three Formula One championships.

1972.race: 145 laps in 1972, the longest of the early runnings
1972.note: Kelleners and Pankl won for Alpina in a BMW 2800 CS, going further than any crew had in the race’s first years.

1971.note: Ferfried Prinz von Hohenzollern and Gerold Pankl won for Alpina in a BMW 2002, the second of the race’s runnings and the first of Pankl’s two consecutive wins.

1970.note: Hans-Joachim Stuck and Clemens Schickentanz won the inaugural race in a BMW 2002 TI for Koepchen BMW Tuning. Stuck won it again in 1998, twenty-eight years later, in a diesel.
